title: Conditionals: elegí la forma correcta
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta. Primero decidí el tipo: ¿siempre verdadero, posible, hipotético o imaginario del pasado?

items.q: If a program ___ an invalid input, it usually returns an error message.
items.e: 'usually' → hecho general → Zero: If + Present Simple, Present Simple.

items.q: If the development team finishes the tests today, they ___ the new version tomorrow.
items.e: Situación posible en el futuro → First: will + base.

items.q: If I ___ more experience with Python, I would apply for that position.
items.e: Hipotético en el presente → Second: If + Past Simple.

items.q: If we had backed up the database, we ___ all that data.
items.e: If + Past Perfect → Third: would have + participio.

items.q: If the server ___ down, users cannot access the application.
If I were the project manager, I ___ the deadline.
items.e: If I were → Second: would + base (no will).

items.q: If they had tested the application properly, they ___ so many bugs after the release.
If the client ___ the design, we will start development next week.
items.e: First Conditional: el if-clause va en Present Simple, nunca will.

items.q: If developers don't use version control, they often ___ track of changes.
If I ___ the lottery, I would travel a lot.
items.e: Poco probable → Second: If + Past Simple (won). Se traduce 'si ganara'.

title: Conditionals: escribí la forma del verbo
instructions: Completá con la forma correcta del verbo entre paréntesis.
text:
1. If the code contains a syntax error, the compiler usually [1] (display) an error message.
2. If we finish the testing phase this week, we [2] (release) the application next Monday.
3. If I were more familiar with JavaScript, I [3] (understand) this code more easily.
4. If we [4] (know) about the server problem earlier, we would have been able to fix it before the presentation.
5. If I had had more time yesterday, I [5] (write) better documentation.
6. If it [6] (rain) tomorrow, we will cancel the trip.
7. If I [7] (win) the lottery, I would travel a lot.
8. If you [8] (heat) ice, it melts.
9. If you had studied, you [9] (pass) the exam.
10. If she [10] (be) here, she would help us.

items.e: Zero: Present Simple en ambas partes; the compiler → displays.
If I were → Second: would + base.
Third: would have + participio (write → wrote → written).
Second: If + Past Simple, no would.
Verdad general: If you heat ice, it melts.
If you had studied → would have passed.
Second: If she were here (forma habitual de to be).

items.q: If the database connection fails, the application displays an error.
If the client approves the design, we will start development next week.
If I were the project manager, I would change the deadline.
If they had tested the application properly, they wouldn't have found so many bugs after the release.
If developers don't use version control, they often lose track of changes.
If it rains, we'll cancel the trip.
If I won the lottery, I would travel a lot.
If I hadn't been sick, I would have gone to your party.
If you heat ice, it melts.
Elegí la correcta:
o: If it will rain, we'll cancel the trip.
If it rains, we'll cancel the trip.
If it rain, we'll cancel the trip.
items.a: If it rains, we'll cancel the trip.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If I would win the lottery, I would travel.
If I won the lottery, I would travel.
If I win the lottery, I would travel.
items.a: If I won the lottery, I would travel.
items.e: Second: if-clause en Past Simple, no would.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If you studied, you would have passed.
If you had studied, you would have passed.
If you would have studied, you would have passed.
items.a: If you had studied, you would have passed.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If I had more money, I will travel.
If I had more money, I would travel.
If I had more money, I would to travel.
items.a: If I had more money, I would travel.
items.e: Second: resultado con would, no will.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If the tests will pass, we'll deploy.
If the tests pass, we'll deploy.
If the tests passed, we'll deploy.
items.a: If the tests pass, we'll deploy.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If we tested the code, we wouldn't have deployed that bug.
If we had tested the code, we wouldn't have deployed that bug.
If we would have tested the code, we wouldn't have deployed that bug.
items.a: If we had tested the code, we wouldn't have deployed that bug.
items.e: Third: had + participio en el if-clause.

items.q: Elegí la correcta:
o: If she were here, she would help us.
If she would be here, she would help us.
If she is here, she would help us.
items.a: If she were here, she would help us.
items.e: Second: If + were/Past Simple, would + base.

title: Third Conditional con modales (might / could have)
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta. would have = seguro; might/could have = posible.

items.q: If it had snowed, it ___ terrible traffic problems.
items.e: Tu apunte: If it had snowed, it might have caused...

items.q: If she had studied more, she ___ a better grade.
If you had been paying attention, you ___ the red traffic light.
items.e: Forma continua en el if-clause + would have + participio (see → saw → seen).

items.q: The result is 100% certain: if we had practised more, we ___ won the match.
items.e: would have = certeza; might/could have = solo posible.

items.q: If it ___ snowed, the roads would have been closed.
If the team ___ the bug earlier, the release could have been on time.
items.e: Pasado imaginario → Past Perfect en el if-clause.

title: Del español al inglés: si pasa / si pasara / si hubiera pasado
instructions: Traducí mentalmente y completá. Recordá: el subjuntivo español ('si ganara', 'si hubieras estudiado') se dice con Past Simple / Past Perfect en inglés.
text:
1. Si ganara la lotería, viajaría mucho: If I [1] (win) the lottery, I [2] (travel) a lot.
2. Si estudiaras, aprobarías el examen: If you [3] (study), you [4] (pass) the exam.
3. Si hubieras estudiado, habrías aprobado: If you [5] (study), you [6] (pass) the exam.
4. Si hubiera testeado el código, no habríamos hecho deploy de ese bug: If we [7] (test) the code, we [8] (not / deploy) that bug.
5. Si los tests pasan, hacemos el deploy: If the tests [9] (pass), we [10] (deploy).

items.e: 'no habríamos hecho deploy' → wouldn't have + participio.
